_comment: Core balance numbers. Values marked in docs/game-design.md are copied here; the rest are playtest guesses. map: size and features of the generated map (seaDepth: rows of sea along the bottom edge, the coast). placement: undo window after building, moving cost (percent of the current price) and demolish refund (percent of what the last copy cost). secondsPerVillagerLeavingOvercrowded: when demolished houses leave more villagers than shelter, one leaves this often. clearing: the cost of turning forest into buildable land; seconds and the rice cost (cost, paid upfront per tile) rise on the gentle curve `growth` (1 + linear·n + quadratic·n², engine/curve.ts) with every tile cleared or queued; each job needs `workers` free villagers (not working in a building); when none are free, clearing borrows from workplaces in `borrow.order` first, then the busiest, never from `borrow.protect` while rice would last less than protectBelowRiceSeconds. military/diplomacy: warriors, battles and the four paths to absorb a neighbor (trade, marriage alliance, sandugo, mangayaw); all placeholders for playtesting. choices: choice events (content/events/choices); minGapSeconds is the 4-minute limit, the start time and chance are playtest guesses. offline: time away credited on return (maxSeconds is the 8-hour cap from docs/game-design.md); the rest only set how coarse, and so how fast, the offline steps are. roads: Daan footpaths (cost per tile, the Connected output bonus for buildings joined to the plaza by an unbroken Daan, and how much faster villagers walk on them, which is visual only); playtest guesses. Raids at the border: raiders land on a river bank, picked among the aiRaid.landingChoices spots nearest the barangay; raiders prefer landing points no staffed Bantayan watches (unwatchedWeight) and coves and river mouths (coveWeight); a watched landing gives a longer warning (rules.watch); the Mandirigma rally at the Kutas and march there (rules.kuta), walking military.warriorTilesPerSecond (forest is slower), and only fight if they get there before the raiders strike. Raids come more at night and dawn and around season changes, less in a typhoon (aiRaid.timing); with allied defenders on their way, winning raiders leave sooner with alliesComingLootPercent of the loot. The player's raids on AI barangays follow the same rules (engine/battle.ts) on the target's generated village, with the landing rolled once per day (Araw), so the visit preview holds; the target's bloc mates come if they arrive within the same warning. aiRaid.lootTargets is where winning raiders go for loot, first one that exists ('kamalig' is listed for when it's built). Playtest guesses. Mandirigma are part-time: they work like any villager except while a raid is coming (they go to meet it) or while away guarding; each Kuta allows military.warriorsPerKuta of them. staffing: below foodFirstBelowRiceSeconds of rice, food workplaces are filled first; the adviser warns once if rice is falling and fewer than foodWorkersWarnPercent of villagers grow food. diplomacy.grudge: how much a neighbor resents the player's raids (raises per raid, decays per minute); at embargoAt they refuse all trade and send no offers; above noAlliancesAbove no marriage or sandugo. tradeDecision: how a neighbor weighs a proposed trade (values per resource, how much trust and grudge shift what they ask, the close-call band decided by a seeded roll, and how far off a deal can be for a counter-offer). handog: peace gifts; value per resource. refusals: what the datu says. Traits' tradeWillingness: traders accept more, proud ones less. Playtest guesses. gatherable: resources the Gather buttons give (gold only comes from Fishing Docks). storage.baseRice: rice the barangay can hold with no Kamalig (each Kamalig adds its own 'storage' from content/buildings, more at each upgrade level). costCurve: each further copy of a building costs base × (1 + linear·n + quadratic·n²) after n copies (engine/curve.ts); tuned with npm run simulate; production and gathering stop at the cap, nothing already stored is lost. Base cap is a playtest guess. happiness: 0-100, starts at `start`, which is also the level that changes nothing; it moves toward a target by pointsPerSecond. The target is start, plus perHouseNearPlaza for every Bahay Kubo within plazaRadius tiles of the plaza (up to maxFromHouses), plus `hungry` while there is no rice, plus perSick for every sick villager (down to maxFromSick). At 100 production is maxEffectPercent higher, at 0 that much lower. Playtest guesses. dayNight: the game's own day (daySeconds of game time; night from nightFrom to nightTo of the day), which the map's tint follows; the Bakunawa eclipse only comes at night. The first eveningShare of the night is the evening, when elders sit with the children by the fire at the datu's clearing (visual; the lessons are rules.population.learning). The moon (drawn small in the HUD beside Araw N, never over the map) goes through its phases every moonCycleDays Araw. worship: offerings at the Dambana turn resources into Favor (offeringValues per resource × favorPerValue, up to maxFavor); changing the barangay's tradition after the first choice costs changeTraditionCost; after neglectAfterSeconds without a ritual, happiness slowly sags by neglectPerMinute up to neglectMax (time away doesn't count); asking permission (permission) costs favorCost Favor and makes the next `tiles` cleared tiles lower Forest Balance by balanceFactor. forest: Forest Balance (0-100) falls by perTile for each forest tile cleared (perTileNearBalete within baleteRadius of a balete, baleteFelled for a balete itself); after quietSeconds with no clearing it recovers by recoveryPerMinute plus recoveryPerForestShare × the share of the map still forest plus recoveryPerBalete per standing balete, each per minute. Below stage1Below anito-of-the-balete pranks (a Woodcutter Camp's tools gone for prankSeconds, prankChancePerSecond) and more tikbalang; below stage2Below the diwata withhold riceWithheldPercent of the rice and sickness is sicknessPercent more likely. replant: turning cleared land back to forest (cost, seconds of one free villager's work, balance gained). All playtest guesses. death: villagers die only with warning and never offline: named villagers grow frail after oldAge.frailAfterSeconds and may then die (chancePerSecond); a sickness that has lasted sickness.afterSeconds with no healer standing may take a sick villager (warning at warnAfterSeconds); after hunger has already driven families away (hunger.afterSeconds of hunger), one villager dies every hunger.everySeconds. mourning: each death adds `seconds` of mourning (up to maxSeconds), during which happiness is `happiness` lower; a Libingan makes it pass faster. Playtest guesses. archipelago: the region's islands (count from min to max, from the seed); blocs: how many rival alliance blocs the AI barangays form at the start, and how many stay independent. sea: Balangay travel: seconds per unit of distance on the regional map (0..1 across), never under minSeconds; boats carry at most raidWarriorsPerBoat warriors. politics: scripted events (content/events/politics), at most one per minGapSeconds, not before startsAfterSeconds; a war costs each member warLossPercent of its warriors every warTickSeconds; invites and join requests need trust (joinTrust) and grudge under maxGrudge; leaving a bloc costs leaveTrustLoss trust with its members, expelling costs expelTrustLoss with the expelled; raiding a bloc member raises the other members' grudge by solidarityPercent of the raid's grudge. allyDefense: allies on the same island arrive in landSeconds plus landSecondsPerUnit × distance; on other islands only allies of at least balangayMinVillagers (who have boats) can come, at sea speed; like the player's own warriors they only fight if they arrive within the raid warning. Tributaries send tributarySendPercent of their warriors when the player is raided. Playtest guesses. kabantugan: renown, earned and never lost; amounts per source (per 10 villagers reached, per task, per raid won attacking or defending, per trade, per tributary or ally gained, per Bahay ng Datu level, per Aklat entry). levelAt: the renown each barangay level from 2 to 20 needs. AI barangays get a level from their size and strength: aiPerVillager × villagers + aiPerStrength × strength, on the same thresholds (retuned with npm run simulate so AI and player levels rise at a similar pace for similar development). Playtest guesses.

battle._comment: How battles end (W.1, engine/warfare.ts), raids both ways. The winner is still decided by attack vs defense; then morale breaks: the beaten side loses loserCasualtyPercent of its warriors, the winner winnerCasualtyPercent (steadier, honored warriors less, up to honorSteadyPercent). Of those hurt, fallenPercent die (feudFallenPercent in a feud's vengeance raid), and of the beaten side's living hurt, captivePercent are held for ransom; the rest are wounded and heal in woundSeconds (faster with a healer's hut). The beaten side breaks when its leader or bravest falls with chance leaderBreakPercent (the report says so). Captives come home after captiveSeconds, or for ransomGoldPerWarrior gold each; AI barangays ransom theirs aiRansomAfterSeconds after the battle if they have the gold. With no Kuta, villagers flee into the forest for hideSeconds when the raiders' attack is fleeAttackRatio times the defense. Playtest guesses, tuned with npm run simulate.

refusals.embargo: {datu} will not trade with you while the memory of your raids is fresh.
refusals.unfair: This trade is unfair to us.
refusals.short: We don't have that much {resource} to give.
refusals.alliance: {datu} will not bind our people to raiders. Make peace first.
refusals.tired: We traded with you only this morning. Come back another day.

stockpile._comment: Soft cap for wood and gold (engine/stockpile.ts), shown in the HUD: multiple × the dearest next big purchase (the next copy of any building the barangay can build, the next Bahay ng Datu or Kamalig level, a Balangay), at least `minimum`. Above it, work brings in slowPercent less of that resource, and above stopMultiple × the cap none at all; nothing stored is lost. Tuned with npm run simulate.

population._comment: Where villagers come from (engine/population.ts). While the barangay is fed and has housing room, newcomers arrive one every secondsPerNewcomer (a reason from content/villagers/arrivals.json; families of up to familyMax), and households in a Bahay Kubo have a child every secondsPerBirth while happiness is at least birthMinHappiness and a couple can be found or formed. Children grow up after childDays game days (Araw) and adults become elders after elderAfterDays. Children don't work and eat childRicePercent of a share; elders work elderWorkPercent of a share (they teach). Newcomers are children or elders by newcomerChildPercent and newcomerElderPercent. The Balita keeps at most balitaMax birth and arrival lines. AI barangays keep the simple arrivals (secondsPerNewVillager). Tuned with npm run simulate so the first 30 minutes grow as before; playtest guesses.

learning._comment: How children learned (engine/talambuhay.ts teach): no school; each evening (as night falls, rules.dayNight.nightFrom) the elders sit with the children by the fire at the datu's gathering place. With chancePerEvening an elder teaches one learner (a child, or a named villager as an apprentice) a lesson from content/villagers/talambuhay.json; it is a dated line in their life story. Children keep at most maxPerChild lessons for when they grow up and are named. Playtest guesses.

residents._comment: Every villager as a person (engine/residents.ts): the share of women, children and elders among new arrivals and births, and of each social class (classPercent: nobility, the warrior class, free commoners, dependents; each tradition names them, content/traditions 'classes'), rolled from the map's seed. Display only (the map's sprites, where they live and work, the villager card); every villager still counts the same in the economy. Class shares are playtest guesses, not historical figures.

healing._comment: Sick villagers stay in the nearest standing healer's hut (engine/healing.ts), at most hutCapacity to a hut; the rest wait at home. Display only: how fast the sick get better still comes from the hut's 'heals' (content/buildings).

plaza._comment: The Bahay ng Datu's footprint, the clearing beside it and the gatherings there (engine/plaza.ts). From bigFromLevel the house takes bigWidth × bigHeight tiles (the plaza tile is its front-left corner: it grows right and back); from reserveFromLevel those extra tiles are kept free of new buildings, Daan and replanting (before that they are ordinary land). A save whose buildings already stand there keeps the one-tile house (the art is drawn within it) until they are gone. Gatherings at the house (idle villagers, workers on a break, warriors called to arms with no Kuta, envoys) stand on open tiles around the house, spotsPerTile to a tile, at most gatherMax at once; the rest wait one tile further out. Display layout, not balance.
plaza._clearing: The clearing beside the house (not a town plaza: those came with Spanish colonial planning): clearingMin..clearingMax open tiles in front of and beside it, seeded per map, kept open and walkable. Display layout, not balance.

aiGrowth._comment: AI barangays clear forest when no free tile is left near their plaza: clearTiles at a time (the same clearing rules and costs as the player). Playtest guess.

eclipse._comment: The Bakunawa challenge (engine/worship.ts gong; the event itself is content/blessings/bakunawa.json). Gong strikes follow a beat every beatSeconds: one within onBeatWindowSeconds of a beat counts onBeat, others offBeat, and a strike sooner than mashGapSeconds after the last counts nothing (mashing doesn't win). With 'hold to beat' (accessibility) the gong sounds on each beat by itself and each counts holdBeat. The strength needed is the event's gongsNeeded plus strengthPerLevel for every barangay level above 1. Villagers strike too: autoStrikes per level of each building listed (a Kuta) and autoPerDatuLevel per Bahay ng Datu level, spread over the event. Playtest guesses.

allyCalls._comment: An ally raided (region.ts): after startsAfterSeconds, each second an aggressive independent barangay may raid one of the player's sandugo allies or bloc mates (chancePerSecond, at most one every cooldownSeconds). A messenger brings a call for help to the Bahay ng Datu (a choice event, content/events/choices/ally-call.json); the raid strikes after warningSeconds. Sending warriors (sendPercent of those at home) fights beside the ally and earns renown and trust; leaving the call unanswered (or saying no) costs ignoreTrust trust with that ally. Playtest guesses.

watch._comment: The Bantayan (engine/watch.ts): a staffed watchtower sees a raid's landing point within radius tiles. A watched raid is seen early: warnings of watchedWarningSeconds, the landing shown from the start and the alarm raised. An unwatched one gives only unwatchedWarningSeconds, and its landing point shows only in the last revealUnwatchedSeconds. Playtest guesses, tuned with npm run simulate.
watch._stakes: Suyak (sharpened bamboo stakes, W.5): each standing one within stakes.radius of the landing slows the raiders secondsEach seconds (up to maxSeconds), so the raid strikes later and the defenders have more time to arrive. Playtest guesses.

tambuli._comment: Calling for help (engine/region.ts callForHelp): during a raid warning the datu may sound the tambuli (a signal fire at night). Allies, bloc mates and tributaries then send armed volunteers on top of their warriors: up to volunteerPercent of their villagers, scaled by how willing they are (their trust out of 100, less distancePenaltyPerUnit for every unit of regional distance). They arrive by the usual arrival rules. Calling for a small raid (attackers at most smallRaidAttackers) or again within cooldownSeconds of the last call costs every answering ally overuseTrust trust. Playtest guesses.

kuta._comment: The Kuta (engine/border.ts muster, engine/region.ts aiRaidStrikes): on the alarm the Mandirigma rally at the Kutas (rallySeconds), then march to the landing; only those who get there before the raiders strike fight, and those with readySeconds to spare get there ready (readyBonus more defense each). Villagers within shelterRadius of a standing Kuta take refuge: if raiders win, they take only shelteredLootPercent of the usual loot from storehouses and fields inside it. Playtest guesses, tuned with npm run simulate.

expeditions._comment: Replays of trades and raids (engine/expeditions.ts): the newest `keep` records are saved; a trade sends `envoys` envoys; a replay draws at most maxSprites people (the report still gives the full counts). Display only, they change no outcome.

limits._comment: Anti-spam (engine/limits.ts). A trade's trust, influence and loyalty are scaled by its value (full at tradeValueFull, at most tradeValueMax times). dailyReturns: what the 1st, 2nd, 3rd, 4th+ trade, Handog or raid with the same barangay on the same day is worth. After fatigueCounterAt trades in a day they want fatigueFairness more; from fatigueRefuseAt they refuse. Marriage needs marriageMinDays since first contact; sandugo needs a marriage or sandugoMinDays. Playtest guesses.

villages._comment: Generated villages of AI barangays (engine/village.ts), by barangay level (from the barangay's renown, on the player's thresholds): each band applies from minLevel. A village shows every building the barangay really has, plus at least the civic buildings its band names (kamalig, fishingDocks, balangayDock, shrine = the babaylan's hut and Dambana, libingan; traders get an extra dock). datuLevel: the Bahay ng Datu drawn; roads: Daan from the plaza to the workplaces; housePaths: houses that get their own Daan. Forest is cleared only as far as the buildings need. Playtest guesses.

food._comment: How a barangay eats (engine/food.ts). Villagers eat Pagkain (foodEatenPerVillagerPerSecond each; children less); with none left they eat Palay, riceWastePercent of a share each (a waste: rice is a prestige good). The datu's household eats datuRicePerLevel Palay a second per Bahay ng Datu level. Where food is kept: root crops stay in the ground (groundPerPlot for each Gabihan or Kaingin; they never spoil and a typhoon can't reach them; drought slows them, see seasonYield); fresh fish, meat, bananas and coconuts spoil (spoilPercentPerMinute) unless kept alive in a Baklad (livePerBaklad) or preserved into household jars (jarsPerHouse per Bahay Kubo) or the Kamalig (its storage.food; the Bahay ng Datu's own kamalig adds datuStorePerLevel). Preserving: each house smokes and dries smokePerHousePerSecond, and salting with Asin preserves saltPreservesPerUnit food per unit of Asin, up to saltPerHousePerSecond a house. People eat fresh food first, then live fish, root crops, and preserved food last. AI barangays keep one simple pool: they eat their Palay above aiRiceReserve first (1:1), then Pagkain, kept up to their jars and Kamalig. Variety: the food groups produced now (starch, fish, meat, fruit and greens) give perGroupHappiness each beyond the first; only one group for monotonySeconds costs monotonyHappiness and makes sickness monotonySickPercent more likely. Kaingin: a plot wears out after fertileHarvest food and must be rested (it returns to forest, +fallowBalance Forest Balance). Over-fishing and over-hunting: a building with 'depletes' wears its area (perUnit for each unit caught, more for each like building within radius), lowering yields by up to maxPenaltyPercent; resting recovers recoveryPerMinute. seasonYield: percent by season and building (rough seas in the habagat months cut fishing; drought cuts rice and gabi; yams, millet and sago hold up). typhoonFreshPercent of fresh food is lost when a typhoon strikes. Playtest guesses, tuned with npm run simulate.

pests._comment: Pests and animals (engine/food.ts updatePests), each warned about and recoverable. Rats eat ratsPercent of the Palay held outside a Kamalig (above what the Kamaligs and the datu's store hold). A swarm of balang (locusts) is seen locustWarningSeconds ahead and then cuts Palayan and Kaingin yields by locustPercent for locustSeconds. Wild boar may trample a field next to the forest (boarSeconds at boarPercent less, and boarStock of the root crops), unless a Bantayan or a hunters' camp stands within boarGuardRadius. Chances are per second, from startsAfterSeconds. Playtest guesses.

feud._comment: Blood debts and feuds (W.2, W.3, engine/feud.ts). Each death adds heatPerDeath × rankWeight to a feud's heat (0-100); it cools coolPerMinute and ends at 0 (very slowly). When the player kills a neighbor's people, that neighbor's grudge rises grudgeOnDeath per death and its bloc mates (kin) trust the player kinTrustLoss less. A neighbor owed blood raids even if it isn't a raider, vengeance.chanceFactor times as often, with warriorsPercent more warriors; a winning vengeance raid sets up to firesMax houses alight; its battles are fierce (rules.military.battle.feudFallenPercent). Making peace: mediation succeeds with chance base + the go-between's own bonus (elder, babaylan, or a neutral datu trusted by both: datuMinTrust) + trustWeight × their trust (0-100) − heatWeight × the feud's heat, in percent; a failed attempt can be retried after retrySeconds. The blood price is per death by rank in each good (gold, Palay, rice wine now; heirlooms can be added as their own resource later); a counter-offer of counterPercent of the price is accepted if within acceptWithinPercent of the asking value. Sealing: a sandugo (with sandugoWine rice wine), a shared Pista (with pistaGifts), or a marriage; sealed peace gives trustBonus and ends the feud; breaking it (raiding them) costs trustLossAll with every barangay and grudge with them. mourningRaid: per second, the chance an AI datu dies and their barangay may go on a mourning raid (Visayan practice; flagged for review). Playtest guesses.

honor._comment: Warriors and honor (W.4, engine/honor.ts): a named warrior earns raidWon for a raid won, defenseWon for a raid beaten off at home, allyDefended for standing with an ally. At each of `levels` honor they reach a new level (a new batok in Visayan barangays, an ornament in others: content/traditions honorMark), noted in their life story, worth renownPerLevel renown. Honored warriors make their side steadier (rules.military.battle.honorSteadyPercent). Playtest guesses.

social._comment: A lively barangay (W.6, engine/social.ts). With at least livelyFreePercent of villagers free (not at work) the evening life gives livelyHappiness (none while mourning); with under tiredFreeBelowPercent free for tiredAfterSeconds, people tire ('Pagod na ang mga tao'): tiredHappiness. Sickness is feastSickPercent likelier during a crowded Pista. Each evening a named villager's story gains a social moment with momentChancePerEvening. Playtest guesses.
